statements.label: supported
statements.text: Mouse DUX and human DUX4 have divergent binding motifs, yet each switches on cleavage-stage embryonic genes, among them MERVL and ERVL-MaLR retrotransposons, in muscle cells of its own species.
statements.evidence: Despite the divergence of their binding motifs, both mouse DUX and human DUX4 in mouse and human muscle cells, respectively, activate genes associated with cleavage-stage embryos, including MERVL and ERVL-MaLR retrotransposons.
statements.note: The abstract states that both factors activate cleavage-stage genes, these retrotransposons included, despite their divergent motifs.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Human DUX4 put into mouse cells still produced modest activation of cleavage-stage genes with conventional promoters, but it did not switch on MERVL-promoted genes.
statements.evidence: We found that human DUX4 expressed in mouse cells maintained modest activation of cleavage-stage genes driven by conventional promoters but did not activate MERVL-promoted genes.
statements.note: This is the experimental result the abstract reports for human DUX4 in a mouse cellular context.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Preventing DUX4 expression in skeletal muscle reverses muscle weakness in people with facioscapulohumeral dystrophy.
statements.evidence: Facioscapulohumeral dystrophy (FSHD; MIM158900, MIM158901) is caused by misexpression of the DUX4 transcription factor in skeletal muscle.
statements.note: The abstract names DUX4 misexpression as the cause of FSHD but reports nothing about suppressing it or about patients' symptoms.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Which retrotransposons are activated tracks with homeodomain divergence between DUX4 and DUX, while the shared ancestral cleavage-stage program is driven from conventional promoters.
statements.evidence: Thus, the ancestral DUX4-regulated genes are characteristic of cleavage-stage embryos and are driven by conventional promoters, whereas divergence of the DUX4 and DUX homeodomains correlates with retrotransposon specificity.
statements.note: The abstract draws exactly this contrast between a conserved conventional-promoter program and divergence-linked retrotransposon specificity.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: ISDra2 TnpB from Deinococcus radiodurans is an RNA-directed nuclease: an RNA from the transposon's right-end element guides it to cut DNA beside a 5'-TTGAT motif.
statements.evidence: Here we show that TnpB of Deinococcus radiodurans ISDra2 is an RNA-directed nuclease that is guided by an RNA, derived from the right-end element of a transposon, to cleave DNA next to the 5'-TTGAT transposon-associated motif.
statements.note: The abstract reports this activity, its guide RNA and the adjacent transposon-associated motif as the study's central finding.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: TnpB proteins encoded by IS607-family insertion sequences cut DNA under RNA guidance just as the ISDra2 enzyme does.
statements.evidence: Insertion sequences of IS200/IS605 and IS607 families 2 are among the simplest mobile genetic elements and contain only the genes that are required for their transposition and its regulation.
statements.note: The IS607 family is introduced as background, but RNA-guided cleavage is demonstrated only for ISDra2 TnpB, so IS607 TnpB activity is left open.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The work confirms experimentally that TnpB is a functional progenitor of CRISPR-Cas nucleases and sets it up as the prototype of a new genome-editing system.
statements.evidence: experimentally confirms that TnpB is a functional progenitor of CRISPR-Cas nucleases and establishes TnpB as a prototype of a new system for genome editing
statements.note: The abstract states both conclusions, turning the earlier bioinformatic prediction of a predecessor relationship into an experimental result.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Reprogrammed TnpB cleaved chosen DNA target sites inside human cells.
statements.evidence: We also show that TnpB could be reprogrammed to cleave DNA target sites in human cells.
statements.note: The abstract reports this retargeting experiment in human cells directly.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: ALS samples carrying known pathogenic mutations fall mainly into the glial activation subtype.
statements.evidence: While several pathogenic mutations have been identified, the vast majority of ALS cases have no family history of disease.
statements.note: The abstract mentions that pathogenic mutations exist but never links mutation status to any of the three molecular subtypes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Machine learning sorted the transcriptomes of 148 postmortem ALS cortex samples into three distinct molecular subtypes.
statements.evidence: Using machine learning algorithms, we stratify the transcriptomes of 148 ALS postmortem cortex samples into three distinct molecular subtypes.
statements.note: The sample count and the three-subtype split are stated as the study's primary result.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The largest subtype, 61% of patient samples, showed oxidative and proteotoxic stress hallmarks, while glial activation signatures predominated in a further 19%.
statements.evidence: The largest cluster, identified in 61% of patient samples, displays hallmarks of oxidative and proteotoxic stress. Another 19% of the samples shows predominant signatures of glial activation.
statements.note: Both proportions and the fact that the stress cluster is the largest are reported in the abstract.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: One group of samples, 20% of the total, combined high retrotransposon expression with signatures of TARDBP/TDP-43 dysfunction.
statements.evidence: Finally, a third group (20%) exhibits high levels of retrotransposon expression and signatures of TARDBP/TDP-43 dysfunction.
statements.note: The abstract characterises the third cluster exactly this way, with its 20% share.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Neural cells lacking TREX1 built up abundant extrachromosomal DNA, much of it originating from endogenous Long Interspersed Element-1 retrotransposons.
statements.evidence: We observed abundant extrachromosomal DNA in TREX1-deficient neural cells, of which endogenous Long Interspersed Element-1 retrotransposons were a major source.
statements.note: The abstract reports the extrachromosomal DNA and names LINE-1 elements as a major source of it.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Loss of TREX1 raised apoptosis in neurons, and the cortical organoids they formed were of reduced size.
statements.evidence: TREX1-deficient neurons also exhibited increased apoptosis and formed three-dimensional cortical organoids of reduced size.
statements.note: Increased apoptosis and smaller organoids are both stated as phenotypes of TREX1-deficient neurons.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In this stem-cell model, reverse-transcriptase inhibitors rescued the neurotoxicity of the AGS neurons and organoids.
statements.evidence: In this model, reverse-transcriptase inhibitors rescued the neurotoxicity of AGS neurons and organoids, highlighting their potential utility in therapeutic regimens for AGS and related disorders.
statements.note: The rescue by reverse-transcriptase inhibitors in the model is reported directly.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: TREX1-deficient microglia add to the neurotoxicity by secreting more type I interferon.
statements.evidence: TREX1-deficient astrocytes further contributed to the observed neurotoxicity through increased type I interferon secretion.
statements.note: Increased interferon secretion is reported for TREX1-deficient astrocytes; the abstract says nothing either way about microglia.
